question: Why does the Transformer scale dot-product attention by 1/sqrt(d_k)?
source_chunk_text: We suspect that for large values of d_k, the dot products grow large in magnitude, pushing the softmax function into regions where it has extremely small gradients. To counteract this effect, we scale the dot products by 1/sqrt(d_k).
ideal_answer: Without scaling, large d_k makes the dot products large in magnitude and the softmax saturates, producing vanishing gradients. Dividing by sqrt(d_k) keeps variance ~1 and gradients usable.

question: What is the role of positional encodings in a Transformer?
source_chunk_text: Since our model contains no recurrence and no convolution, in order for the model to make use of the order of the sequence, we must inject some information about the relative or absolute position of the tokens in the sequence.
ideal_answer: Transformers have no recurrence or convolution, so they cannot infer token order intrinsically. Positional encodings inject absolute or relative position information so attention can attend order-dependently.
